content.text: So quick review (and I'll need to do alot more reading), but version 5 removes a command line interface. Which is probably okay because we just want to use it from inside the existing applications.
However version 5 also no longer supports directly serializing a bag. They do provide example code for how we could implement it ourselves.
ie. zip
https://github.com/LibraryOfCongress/bagit-java/blob/master/src/test/java/gov/loc/repository/bagit/examples/serialization/CreateZipBagExample.java
or tar
https://github.com/LibraryOfCongress/bagit-java/blob/master/src/test/java/gov/loc/repository/bagit/examples/serialization/CreateTarBagExample.java
I started poking around with the LC bagit-java library, and found it was pretty easy to build a bag on disk:
https://gist.github.com/escowles/13306ce01dc557d92aa5f9641fc7afce

I think this could work well with the exporter, where we'd setup the Bag at the beginning of the export, add each file to the Bag as we wrote its description to disk (to get the SHA1), and then finalize the Bag at the end of the export.
Sounds like this is a win then
shall we keep this open given
https://github.com/LibraryOfCongress/bagit-java/issues/72
and 5.0.0-RC10, and hash out requirements for walking away from that library?

Yes, I think should keep this ticket open and continue to assess whether we should go forward with LoC's bagit-java.  Between the JavaFX issue, and the general response to our tickets, I think it's an open question whether it's a good fit.
Removing bagit-java and implementing our own BagIt support makes our code simpler, and removed dependency on JavaFX:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export/pull/68
Resolved with:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export/commit/626223a13e5c98fa2a914260528f59e6370ee5de
Evaluate the Library of Congress BagIt Library:
https://github.com/LibraryOfCongress/bagit-java
Key priorities are:
Avoid reading data twice when adding files to Bags
Does it support serializing Bags as e.g., Zip or Tar files?
